doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Born in Chicago and first hearing music at Reverend Turner's church
summary: Ware, born 1923, lives with Reverend Turner and his wife next door to a sanctified church; he hears the band, gets a toy drum, and sees Turner play piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You were born in Chicago on September 8, 1923, the only son of Elijah Roger Bernard and Eleanor Broomfield Ware. Tell us when you became aware of music.

I became aware of music, maybe my 3rd or 4th year. By that I mean I was about 4 years old. There was a sanctified church next door to where we were living. I was living with my great aunt and my mother, and her children; my great aunt's children -- and this lady next door, they didn't have no children; Reverend Turner and his wife Della. I used to go over and have cookies and milk and whatnot.
And they had church services -- I can remember well; it was in the summer, and they had a band in there, and I can't say what instruments they Ware brought because I didn't recognize them.

but it was so joyful; I mean, the singing and the band playing, and it got so that Reverend Turner and his wife would take me over to the church nightly, and eventually I started living with Reverend Turner. They didn't adopt me, but my mother being young, and my father and her having split up ... so I was kind of raised by Reverend Turner.
And that was my first introduction to music. I guess around that time, radio was becoming kind of popular. I remember listening to that old show, Amos and Andy -- and to hear Amos sing "Am I Blue".

Well about that time, Mrs. Turner bought me a toy drum, and I'd go to church with her with the drum. I'd be in the benches -- I wouldn't be on the rostrum, naturally, I was quite young -- I don't think I was but 5; I don't remember well because I was going to something like a nursery school; I wasn't yet in kindergarten. And I remember that Reverend Turner had a piano up at his house, and an old C Melody saxophone and a couple of guitars, and they had -- they always had music going on.

Mrs. Turner, she played a little guitar. Reverend Turner would sit down and play at the piano, and I don't know to this day whether he had any musical education, but he knew how to play -- and he taught me little things.
So that was my first introduction; had to be in the 20's or the latter 20's.
